messages.subject: Language manual section 16.3
parts:
In section 16.3 on functions accessing the log_prob accumulator, there's this example which the document says:


Here is an example of a function to return the centered coefficients derived from a
non-centered vector of parameters beta_raw along with the location mu of the center
and the scale sigma; see Section 19.1 for more information on centering.

Here's the example:

functions {
  vector center_lp(vector beta_raw, real mu, real sigma) {
    beta_raw ~ normal(0,1);
    sigma ~ cauchy(0,5);
    mu ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
    return sigma * beta_raw + mu;
  }
}


To me it looks like the first thing that happens is a call to:

normal_log(beta_raw,0,1)

So I'm confused but here's my interpretation:  after sampling beta_raw will look like it has a distribution N(0,1)... which means the function
is in fact using a centered parameterization of (random) effects along with a mean and standard deviation to produce a vector of non-centered
coefficients for use in regression.

Am I right about this?  If so, could the documentation be re-written to emphasize the effect of using such a function? Something along
the lines of

Here is an example of a function to assign standard normal priors to a vector of coefficients, along with a center and scale, and return the
translated and scaled coefficients.  It can be used to generate transformed parameters while maintaining a centered parameterization.

What I'm really trying to do is sort out the meaning of this code: becs.aalto.fi/en/research/bayes/diabcvd/wei_lap_joint.stan

... but the manual has me confused.

Thanks for any clarification,

Krzysztof

> coefficients for use in regression.

No. The terminology in the literature is confusing.
The beta_raw has a NON-centered parameterization and the
return value of the function will be centered around mu (at
least if nothing else is going on in the model).

It's what we used to call the "Matt trick" because Matt Hoffman independently
suggested it before we realized there was a literature on it.

> If so, could the documentation be re-written to emphasize the effect of using such a function? Something along
> the lines of
>
> Here is an example of a function to assign standard normal priors to a vector of coefficients, along with a center and scale, and return the
> translated and scaled coefficients. It can be used to generate transformed parameters while maintaining a centered parameterization.

I think your formulation is clearer. And it needs a cross-ref to
the section of the manual talking about centered and non-centered
parameterizations!
